lead.headline: SBI Bets $270M on Ajaib as Asian Financial Conglomerates Race to Own Digital Asset Infrastructure
lead.tldr: Traditional finance is no longer experimenting with crypto—it is building the rails to dominate it, while network security failures expose the gap between institutional-grade infrastructure and DeFi's operational fragility.

intro: Dear Founders, Investors, and Friends, this week the capital deployment patterns of Asia's largest financial groups clarified where the value is actually accruing in digital assets, and it is not where most venture dollars are currently flowing.

top_signals.title: Cronos halts network after Tectonic exploit involving estimated $75M33m, Cronos halts network after Tectonic exploit involving estimated $75MCrypto.com CEO Kris Marszalek said the company’s app and exchange were unaffected by the Tectonic breach and continued operating normally.
top_signals.summary: The Cronos network was halted following a security exploit on the Tectonic protocol involving an estimated $75 million. Crypto.com CEO Kris Marszalek clarified that the company's exchange and app remain unaffected and operational.
top_signals.why_it_matters: A $75 million exploit triggering a full network halt on Cronos demonstrates that chain-level operational resilience remains materially underpriced by investors underwriting DeFi exposure.

top_signals.title: SBI Holdings invests $270 million in Ajaib, taking 20% stake amid Asia digital asset push
top_signals.summary: SBI Holdings has invested $270 million to acquire a 20% stake in Ajaib, a digital asset platform. This move is part of SBI's broader strategy to expand its digital asset footprint across Asia.
top_signals.why_it_matters: SBI's $270 million for 20% of Ajaib signals that Asian financial conglomerates now prefer equity stakes in regulated distribution platforms over direct token holdings, repricing where infrastructure rents will be captured.

top_signals.title: Mirae Asset maps out $109 billion digital asset push with Digital X: report
top_signals.summary: South Korean financial giant Mirae Asset is planning a massive digital asset expansion centered around its Digital X initiative. The firm aims to build a $109 billion business in the sector with a goal of achieving profitability by 2027.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Mirae Asset's $109 billion Digital X target, with a profitability deadline of 2027, gives investors a testable benchmark for when tokenized asset infrastructure must show unit economics or face capital reallocation.

top_signals.title: SEC sends crypto custody rule overhaul to White House for review
top_signals.summary: The SEC has sent a proposed overhaul of its decades-old custody requirements to the White House for review. This move, pushed by Paul Atkins, aims to provide clearer regulatory frameworks for the custody of digital assets.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Paul Atkins pushing custody rule modernization to the White House indicates the regulatory arbitrage window for non-qualified custodians is closing, which will reprice competitive moats for incumbents who invested early in compliance infrastructure.

top_signals.title: Kalshi raised $1.12 billion via private equity offering since April, latest SEC filing shows
top_signals.summary: Kalshi has raised $1.12 billion through private equity offerings since April, according to recent SEC filings. The company is reportedly seeking an additional $750 million in capital at a $40 billion valuation.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Kalshi's $1.12 billion raise since April and pursuit of $750 million more at $40 billion demonstrates that prediction market infrastructure is being valued as a regulated derivatives venue, not a crypto novelty, with implications for how we underwrite event-contract protocols.

top_signals.title: India plans first tokenized bonds using wholesale CBDC: Report20m
top_signals.summary: India is planning to launch its first tokenized bonds utilizing a wholesale Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC). This move aims to modernize the bond market and improve settlement efficiency through blockchain technology.
top_signals.why_it_matters: India's wholesale CBDC-linked tokenized bonds represent a G20 economy choosing to run its sovereign debt infrastructure on distributed ledgers, which validates the settlement-efficiency thesis but also crowds out private-sector alternatives.

deals.summary: SBI Holdings has invested $270 million to acquire a 20% stake in Ajaib, a digital asset platform. This move is part of SBI's broader strategy to expand its digital asset footprint across Asia.

Kalshi has raised $1.12 billion through private equity offerings since April, according to recent SEC filings. The company is reportedly seeking an additional $750 million in capital at a $40 billion valuation.

BitGo has acquired the institutional trading arm of NYDIG to strengthen its institutional crypto offerings. The deal includes the acquisition of approximately 30 employees and existing client relationships, focusing on expanding derivatives and financing services.

Bitfinex Securities has successfully completed a $50 million tokenized capital raise for Alkemya. The funding was achieved through the issuance of ALKN, a tokenized security representing limited partnership interests.
Stablecoin neobanking platform Fasset has raised $68 million in a Series C funding round led by SBI Group. This investment values the company at $1 billion, marking its transition to unicorn status.

French Bitcoin treasury firm Capital B has raised $24.5 million through a private placement to expand its BTC holdings. The round saw participation from notable figures including BlockStream's Adam Back and TOBAM, with potential for further funding via warrants.

on_the_radar.title: Russia’s Sber eyes USDT loans, questions digital ruble demand10m, Russia’s Sber eyes USDT loans, questions digital ruble demandRussia’s largest bank, Sber, plans to accept USDT and Ether alongside Bitcoin as loan collateral as the country introduces regulated crypto trading under a new law.
on_the_radar.summary: Russia's largest bank, Sber, intends to accept USDT, Ether, and Bitcoin as collateral for loans. This move coincides with the introduction of new laws to regulate cryptocurrency trading within the country.

on_the_radar.title: Stablecoins not credible for payments at scale, BIS chief says
on_the_radar.summary: The head of the Bank for International Settlements (BIS) has stated that stablecoins lack the credibility required for large-scale payment systems. He instead advocates for the use of tokenized bank deposits as a superior alternative for everyday transactions.

on_the_radar.title: Solana validators approve proposal to accelerate SOL disinflation
on_the_radar.summary: Solana validators have approved its first binding governance vote to accelerate the disinflation of the SOL token supply. The proposal passed after Kraken shifted its position from opposition to support.

on_the_radar.title: Bullish provides USD.AI $100M stablecoin facility for GPU-backed lending
on_the_radar.summary: Bullish has provided a $100 million stablecoin facility to USD.AI to support lending backed by GPU infrastructure. This move highlights the growth of onchain private credit specifically targeting AI computing resources.

on_the_radar.title: Bitwise fund is first Solana ETF to hit $1 billion AUM
on_the_radar.summary: The Bitwise Solana Staking ETF (BSOL) has become the first Solana ETF to reach $1 billion in assets under management. This milestone was achieved in less than a year since the fund's launch.

on_the_radar.title: Visa works with Upbit parent on stablecoin payments, AI commerce40m
on_the_radar.summary: Visa is collaborating with the parent company of Upbit to integrate stablecoin payments and AI-driven commerce solutions. This partnership aims to bridge traditional financial infrastructure with digital asset payment rails.

on_the_radar.title: Dunamu and Visa partner on stablecoin, AI business; Open Standard's OUSD under consideration
on_the_radar.summary: Dunamu and Visa have entered a partnership to explore business opportunities involving stablecoins and artificial intelligence. The collaboration is specifically considering the integration of Open Standard's OUSD for future use cases.

on_the_radar.title: Abu Dhabi royal backs 49% stake in Trump-linked crypto bank venture: WSJ11m, Abu Dhabi royal backs 49% stake in Trump-linked crypto bank venture: WSJSheikh Tahnoon’s group reportedly backs a 49% stake in the holding company behind World Liberty’s conditionally approved US trust bank.
on_the_radar.summary: A group led by Abu Dhabi royal Sheikh Tahnoon is reportedly backing a 49% stake in the holding company for World Liberty's conditionally approved US trust bank. This venture links high-profile political figures and Middle Eastern capital to the US crypto banking sector.

on_the_radar.title: XRP treasury firm Evernorth says SEC registration now effective, clearing way for Nasdaq listing
on_the_radar.summary: XRP treasury firm Evernorth has announced that its SEC registration is now effective, paving the way for a Nasdaq listing. The listing will be achieved through a merger with the SPAC firm Armada.

on_the_radar.title: Virtu, Tradeweb complete onchain repo using Marshall Islands digital bond7m
on_the_radar.summary: Virtu and Tradeweb have successfully completed an on-chain repurchase agreement (repo) utilizing a digital bond issued by the Marshall Islands. This marks a significant step in the integration of traditional financial instruments with blockchain technology.

on_the_radar.title: Charles Schwab adda Solana, Avalanche and Chainlink to nascent crypto platform
on_the_radar.summary: Charles Schwab is expanding its nascent crypto platform by adding support for Solana, Avalanche, and Chainlink. This move extends the firm's direct trading offerings beyond the initial support for Bitcoin and Ether.

on_the_radar.title: Bank of England set for new innovation mandate covering stablecoins
on_the_radar.summary: The UK government is introducing a new innovation mandate for the Bank of England to modernize payment systems. This move is specifically aimed at advancing stablecoin regulations and enhancing cross-border cooperation with the United States.

linkedin_post:
SBI Holdings now owns 20% of Ajaib and just led a separate $68 million round for Fasset at a billion-dollar valuation. Mirae Asset wants a $109 billion digital asset business by 2027. The pattern is not subtle: Asian financial conglomerates are buying the distribution layer, not the tokens.

We have spent years underwriting protocols on the assumption that open infrastructure would capture value from incumbents. The reverse is happening. SBI and Mirae are not accumulating governance tokens or staking yields. They are taking equity in the regulated pipes that retail and institutional flows will actually use, with compliance built in and balance-sheet capacity to absorb volatility.

This reprices the venture opportunity set sharply. The wrapper matters more than the underlying asset. Coinbase's tokenized stock entry, built on third-party wrappers with unclear beneficial ownership, confirms that even the most sophisticated US players are still negotiating this same abstraction layer.

The testable thesis: by 2027, the majority of tokenized asset volume will clear through vertically integrated platforms owned by banks and brokers, not through decentralized protocols. Mirae's profitability deadline gives us the marker. If Digital X is not materially contributing to Mirae's bottom line by then, the infrastructure buildout was premature and the capital intensity was mispriced.

Cronos halting its network after a $75 million exploit, Fogo freezing after an attacker took 10% of supply—these are not exceptions. They are the baseline risk that institutional capital will pay a premium to avoid. The premium is going to regulated equity in regulated entities.

We are reweighting our Asia pipeline toward distribution and custody infrastructure. The tokens can wait.
